business_scope.primary_industry_name: Direct Online Retail of Portable Battery Generators and Solar Panels

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law for Quebec private commercial law; Common Law for federal public, criminal and regulatory law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Agreement between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (Canada–China FIPA, 2014)
Convention between Canada and the United States of America with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, S.O.R./2002-184; Special Economic Measures Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. S-14; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2. Quebec: Act respecting the verification of the beneficial owners of an enterprise, CQLR c. V-2.2.1; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Certificate of Good Standing for each corporate general partner or foreign corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address for all general partners, limited partners, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of foreign-language incorporation documents and financial statements (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified translator in Quebec or notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and translator's certificate (no apostille required for the translation itself)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney / Mandate for the designated Quebec registration agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or consular office in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners, and UBOs against Canadian and UN consolidated sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act sanctions, FINTRAC reporting requirements, and domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEP) databases. Enhanced due diligence required for high-risk jurisdictions, crypto-linked activity, or partners from FATF-high-risk countries. Re-screening must occur upon material changes in ownership, new sanctions designations, or regulatory trigger events.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the declared name must be in French and conform to French grammatical rules. A version in another language may be used only when a French version is also permanently shown on signs and in the enterprise's legal records. Transliteration into Latin script is required; names using non-Latin scripts must be romanized consistently and the French form must be distinct and compliant.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Quebec, Québec, Canada (when implying governmental sponsorship or authority)
Corporation, société par actions (unless the legal form is appropriate)
Terms suggesting illegal activity or public disorder
Terms that are misleading, too general, or not sufficiently distinctive
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the notice, attaching legal submissions and evidence of compliance. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the civil division of the Court of Québec in the district where the registered office is located. Alternatively, the applicant may promptly submit a new name reservation request with a modified name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for low-risk e-commerce retail if the virtual office provider maintains a physical address in Quebec, offers mail forwarding, and accepts service of process. A P.O. box alone is not sufficient. The limited partnership must maintain its books and records at the registered office or another place specified in its declaration of registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% probability of unannounced on-site inspection within the first year for this low-risk retail activity; probability may rise to 20% if foreign partners or sanctions-triggering jurisdictions are present.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation request fee with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
Initial declaration of registration of the limited partnership
Notarization, apostille/consular legalization of foreign UBO and corporate documents (three documents at approximately USD 200 each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent authentication authority (Global Affairs Canada or consulate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for notarial and legalization services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of foreign incorporation documents and supporting records
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark per translation unit

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Virtual office and registered office services (12 months)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered office / virtual office service provider in Quebec

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO verification, PEP/sanctions screening, and AML/CFT compliance file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional fee based on complexity and risk review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence, drafting of limited partnership agreement, and corporate governance consultation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Professional fee at prevailing market rates for cross-border commercial work

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, Book IV, Title II, Articles 2236-2264 (Limited Partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c P-44.1), sections 17-18; Business Corporations Act (RLRQ c S-31.1) for the corporate general partner.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration of a Limited Partnership (Declaration d'immatriculation de societe en commandite) filed through the Registraire's online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is imposed for a Quebec limited partnership. The initial capital contribution is freely fixed in the limited partnership agreement and may be made in money, property, or services. No statutory escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER - CA-QUEBEC LP WHEREAS [General Partner Inc.] is the general partner of [Name] limited partnership to be formed under Article 2236 of the Civil Code of Quebec; WHEREAS the Limited Partnership will engage in online retail of portable battery generators and solar panels; NOW IT IS RESOLVED: 1. The General Partner subscribes to an initial capital contribution in the amount of CDN $10,000 as stipulated in the limited partnership agreement. 2. The registered office of the Limited Partnership is established at [full address, Quebec]. 3. Appointment of [Name] as initial manager and [Name] as secretary/treasurer is ratified. 4. Signing officers are authorized to file the declaration with the Registraire and to execute ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reserved Name Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec — online name evaluation service (Evaluation du nom)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name declaration for the proposed limited partnership and for the corporate general partner using the Registraire's online service. Include the corporate name, statutory descriptors, and a precise business activity description. Await the name evaluation result, which carries a binding character for reuse in the registration declaration.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and legal suffix
Business activity description (ISIC 4791 / Quebec NAICS 443142)
Authorization or corporate resolution of the applicant
Registration evidence for the general partner if already existing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file an amended name declaration through the same online service within 10 days, preserving the distinctive component and avoiding any reproduction of a protected trade name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil-law notary or qualified legal counsel — no government filing required
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Contrat de societe en commandite setting out the partnership's nature, capital contributions, profit-sharing, decision-making rights, and liability allocation between general and limited partners. Execute the agreement in written form before signature and securely retain the original.
required_dossiers: Identity and address of each general and limited partner
Capital contribution schedule (cash, property, and services)
Profit, loss, and distribution allocation provisions
Term of partnership and withdrawal, dissolution, and transfer provisions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Execute a supplementary deed of amendment to correct any inconsistencies with the Civil Code of Quebec; re-execute with notarized signatures if required by a bank or major creditor.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec — online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration d'immatriculation in the Registre des entreprises du Quebec. Provide the full legal name, registered address in Quebec, complete list of general and limited partners, roles, and the corporate general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation. Pay the prescribed filing fee online and obtain the Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration form
Copy of the executed limited partnership agreement
Certificate of corporate existence or legalization for the general partner
Name evaluation result and signatory authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any notice of deficiency from the Registraire within 20 days; correct omitted partner data and re-submit the declaration without delay. Late fees are assessed if correction exceeds the prescribed period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Quebec Tax and Payroll Accounts with Revenu Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Quebec — Online Business Services (Mon compte d'entreprise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the NEQ to register for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and, if employing staff, register for source deductions and payroll obligations. Complete the employer registration with the Commission des normes, de l'equite, de la sante et de la securite du travail (CNESST) for workers' compensation coverage.
required_dossiers: NEQ of the limited partnership
Business activity description and expected annual turnover statement
Names, addresses, and social insurance numbers of directors or managers if hiring employees
Bank account attestation for direct debit or electronic payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, submit a written response to Revenu Quebec's Client Services with a corrected LM-1-V form and supporting incorporation documents. Re-file within 10 business days to avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Physical Site Compliance and Municipal Licensing Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality and municipal fire safety authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office and any distribution location are zoned for commercial online retail and limited warehouse storage of lithium-ion batteries. Coordinate a fire safety inspection for battery storage, obtain municipal occupancy approval, and verify compliance with Quebec consumer display and virtual storefront requirements.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership proof of the registered office
Municipal zoning compliance certificate or permit application
Fire safety inspection request with battery storage quantity declaration
Website consumer information draft showing the business name, NEQ, and full Quebec address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal inspection identifies deficiencies, implement required fire suppression and storage containment measures, provide proof of corrective action, and re-apply for clearance. Any denial may be appealed to the municipal zoning committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing or physical operating license is required for direct online retail of portable power equipment. Product compliance authorities include Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) and Health Canada for electrical and battery consumer safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating or manufacturing permit is required for the described e-commerce retail activity; import and distribution must comply with the Canada Consumer Product Safety Act and Transport Canada's Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations for lithium batteries.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable for a retail-only activity; should future assembly or battery repair operations be added, consultation with Quebec's Ministere de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques (MELCCFP) will be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no industrial discharge, no atmospheric emission generating process, and no manufacturing installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC emission points exist for online retail. Waste lithium-ion batteries must be managed in accordance with Quebec's Regulation respecting hazardous materials and applicable take-back obligations under the Regulation on the recovery of certain products.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the competent municipal fire service is required for any warehouse space storing lithium-ion batteries. Structural load and layout must satisfy municipal occupancy bylaws. Occupational health and safety clearance is addressed through self-assessment of emergency exits, electrical installations, and storage practices under the Act respecting occupational health and safety; CNESST employer registration is mandatory once employees are hired.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — My Business Account and GST/HST Internet Filing Service; Provincial: Revenu Québec — e-services portal for Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) registration and filing.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain a nine-digit Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) by submitting Form RC1; Step 2: Activate the GST/HST program account (RT) through the same registration, selecting the Canadian activity as 'online retail of portable power equipment'; Step 3: Register with Revenu Québec for a QST account using the online business registration service or Form LM-1, providing the federal BN and Quebec establishment address; Step 4: If the limited partnership has no physical Quebec presence, appoint a responsible natural person located in Quebec or Canada as the authorized contact/agent for tax administration; Step 5: Retain the partnership resolution and constituent LLP/LP declaration to evidence the entity's authority to bind the partnership for GST/QST filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — a Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent under federal and Quebec law: income, gains, losses, and credits flow to the partners. For GST/HST and QST administration, the partnership itself may be registered as a registrant in its own capacity, but it is not a taxpayer for income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style 'check-the-box' election. A limited partnership cannot elect to be treated as a corporation; pass-through status under section 96 of the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act (Quebec) is mandatory. No hybrid-mismatch entity election is available internally. For cross-border treaty purposes, the LP remains transparent and may be treated as an intermediate flow-through entity under applicable double-taxation conventions, subject to the specific foreign tax law characterization.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Canada value-added sales tax) and Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), a separate provincial VAT-style consumption tax administered by Revenu Québec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide gross taxable supplies over the immediately preceding four calendar quarters for federal GST/HST small-supplier relief; the Quebec QST registration threshold is likewise CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Quebec over the same four-quarter lookback period. The threshold applies to all revenue channels, including online marketplace sales, unless the marketplace itself is the deemed supplier.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory government API clearance, or digital tax stamping is in force for GST/HST or QST. CRA and Revenu Québec accept standard electronic invoices in accessible formats (PDF/XML); taxpayers must preserve complete transactional records in legible electronic form. Businesses may voluntarily use PEPPOL-compliant e-invoicing, but there is no mandatory clearance before invoice issuance for standard B2B or B2C exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% GST/HST rate applies to tangible personal property exported from Canada when the supplier or its delivering agent ships the goods outside Canada under an export sale, possession and risk of loss pass outside Canada, and the goods are not acquired for consumption/use in Canada. Portable solar generators and panels sold online to foreign customers qualify as zero-rated exports when physically shipped abroad, including courier fulfilment. QST zero-rating follows the same destination principle under Quebec rules. Offshore services qualify only if performed entirely outside Canada or directly incidental to an exported supply; remote digital assistance must be tested separately for place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA B13A) or the applicable authorized export report filed through the Canadian Automated Export Declaration/AES system for goods leaving Canada by commercial shipment.
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / final carrier invoice showing the goods departed Canada and were delivered to the foreign destination address.

Inward Remittance Certificate / foreign payment bank credit evidence linking the customer's remittance to the corresponding export invoice (retained as audit corroboration of the cross-border commercial settlement).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess export zero-rating claims within the normal four-year reassessment period, and indefinitely where misrepresentation or fraud is established. If the export documentation is incomplete or the transaction is recharacterized as a domestic supply, the full GST/HST and QST become payable on the selling price, with compound interest and late-filing penalties. Deliberately false export declarations may attract gross-negligence penalties and criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec taxation statutes, with retrospective clawback of any input tax credits claimed on purchases attributable to the export supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange transactions are monitored indirectly through the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CFT reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both capital and current accounts with no general exchange-control legislation. Profit remittances by non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (25% unless reduced by treaty) and Canadian partnership reporting requirements, but no central bank approval is required for conversion or transfer of funds. Quebec imposes additional provincial registration and reporting obligations, not FX approval.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no export proceeds surrender rules, no statutory conversion timelines, and no mandatory conversion ratio. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency bank accounts within Canada or abroad, subject to FINTRAC transaction reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000 or equivalent) and deemed tax residency provisions for controlled foreign corporations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Regulated Canadian EMIs and payment service providers such as Wise (TransferWise), Payoneer, and Nuvei offer multi-currency settlement for cross-border ecommerce disbursements, but they are not substitutes for tier-1 banking in Quebec. The Canadian Retail Payment Activities Act requires registration for payment service providers handling Canadian CAD clearing; foreign EMIs without Canadian registration may only support non-CAD corridors with limited AML counterparty coverage.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement for directors to appear physically in Canada to open a corporate bank account. Most Schedule I banks accept remote video KYC for entities with verified general partners and an existing Canadian corporate registry profile (Quebec Registraire des entreprises). However, fully remote onboarding without a Canada-based signatory or physical office triggers enhanced due diligence, and some banks (e.g., National Bank of Canada) may require an in-person interview at a Quebec branch for partnerships with foreign partners. Notarized copies of identification, apostilled partnership agreement, and beneficial ownership declarations are generally mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partner with no Canadian residential address or passport lacking tax residency certification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passport copy; proof of residential address in home country; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Form NR3010 (Declaration of Non-Residency); certified copies of the partnership agreement showing the partner's 25% or greater beneficial interest; IPSA or equivalent background check report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection originating from a high-risk jurisdiction or unaudited investment company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter issued within last 90 days; source of wealth statement certified by an attorney or public accountant; six months of bank statements showing the origin of funds; signed sworn declaration of legal source of funds; chain-of-title documentation for corporate shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High transaction volumes inconsistent with a newly formed portable power ecommerce retailer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro forma financial projections approved by a CPA; commercial contracts with major suppliers (solar panel OEMs, logistics providers); marketplace or Stripe/PayPal settlement history for pre-registration operations; inventory warehouse lease agreement; FINTRAC large transaction report templates filed by the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a third-party payment processor (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) that may obscure underlying transaction details
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Processor agreements with clear settlement structure; merchant ID and PCI DSS compliance certificates; daily sales and refund reconciliation files; chargeback and dispute resolution procedures; assignment of rights ensuring the bank can access transaction-level data for AML review.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols require inbound partner equity contributions to be routed via SWIFT MT103 (single payment) or MT202 COV (cover payment) to the partnership's Canadian operational account. For statistical and tax clarity, the remittance information field must reference 'Contribution under Limited Partnership Agreement [date]' and the purpose code 'Direct Investment in Canada' (BOP Code 100/300). The bank will require a completed Beneficiary Ownership and Source of Funds declaration, plus, for amounts above CAD 10,000, FINTRAC reporting triggers. Quebec's Registraire des entreprises may require filing of changes in capital structure if the injection exceeds partnership registry thresholds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement for imports of solar panels and generators should use SWIFT MT103 via Canadian correspondent banks for cross-border supplier payments. For bulk purchases, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by a Canadian Schedule I bank is recommended; the LC requires a pro forma invoice, packing list, bill of lading, and certificate of origin. Domestic CAD disbursements (warehousing, logistics, payment processors) clear through Payments Canada (Real-Time Rail, ACSS) with no FX exposure. Cross-border CAD/foreign payments may be settled via SWIFT gpi or FX Direct clearing through correspondent networks.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX Forwards (up to 24 months) for CAD/USD and CAD/EUR exposure
FX Swaps (spot-forward combinations) to manage rolling inventory costs
FX Options (collared and participating) for loss-limited hedging

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not generally available for CAD due to full convertibility; where an NDF is offered for CAD-adjacent emerging market currencies, the Bank of Canada's published reference rates may be used for valuation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registration update (mise à jour) with the Quebec Enterprise Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within 6 months after the end of the partnership's fiscal year (if none, within 6 months after the registration anniversary)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD $10 per day, up to CAD $500; repeated non-filing may lead to administrative dissolution or strike-off of the LP's registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership information return (TP-600 / T5013 slip filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the partnership's fiscal year-end (tax year), generally March 15 for associated T5013 slips
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty for failing to file T5013/TP-600: CAD $25 per slip per day, minimum CAD $100, plus late-filing penalties under federal and Quebec tax laws; criminal prosecution in severe cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not statutorily required for a private limited partnership unless the partnership agreement mandates an audit, the LP is a 'reporting issuer' under the Quebec Securities Act, or the LP meets the federal 'large partnership' threshold (average annual gross revenue exceeding CAD $20 million or total assets exceeding CAD $10 million).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS if the LP is a publicly accountable enterprise; otherwise ASPE (Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) or a chosen general purpose framework under CPA Canada

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LP must confirm and update its ultimate beneficiaries (registered direct or indirect owners of 25% or more of the partnership) annually via the Quebec Enterprise Register. Any ownership transfer during the year must be reported within 30 days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined general corporate rate (federal 15% + Quebec 11.5%); Canadian Limited Partnerships are fiscally transparent and pay no entity-level income tax
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Small Business Deduction (9% federal rate on first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation partner; Quebec SME rate 5%, scheduled to reduce to 3.2%, on the same CAD 500,000 base); the LP itself is a flow-through, so eligible SR&ED expenditure pools are allocated to partners and the refundable 35% SR&ED investment tax credit is claimed at the partner level; no separate Quebec tax holiday exists for e-commerce retailers
